solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Consider old hat what a jockey must do before a race

definitions.text: what a jockey must do before a race

parts.note: to weigh something up is to consider it
something old hat is out of fashion, or simply out

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about stale thinking, then a description of race-day routine for riders.
explanation.walkthrough: Before a race a jockey is weighed with the saddle to check the horse carries the right weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Jockeys must be checked on the scales before racing so that each horse carries its allotted burden.

clue.text: To rub out is simplicity once end of rubber's employed

indicators.note: the letter is employed, put to work inside the word for simplicity

parts.note: ease means simplicity, as in doing something with ease

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word rubber

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A note on how effortless erasing becomes once a rubber is put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' and 'is' are link words; 'employed' signals the R going into EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to remove marks, a synonym of rubbing them out.

clue.text: Various sugar lumps surrounding round dish

indicators.note: surrounding means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
various suggests the letters of sugar lumps arranged in a different order

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A dessert dish served with assorted sugar lumps around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is slang for a very attractive person, not food: the anagram of SUGAR LUMPS goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for an alluring, attractive person, just as a glamour puss is a showily attractive one.

clue.text: Cartoon character may be dressing when broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the words for the dressing are taken by their sound

parts.note: olive oil is a salad dressing

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a cartoon figure could be a salad dressing once it is on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Popeye's girlfriend in the cartoons has a name pronounced like the salad oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye's lanky sweetheart is a long-running animated cartoon figure.

clue.text: You have to satisfy every requirement if exile blocks that abroad

indicators.note: abroad means all over the place, so the letters are scattered and reordered

explanation.surface: An official reminder that exiles must meet every condition before being blocked from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You have to' and 'if' are link words; the fifteen letters of EXILE BLOCKS THAT rearrange to give the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: On a checklist form each condition met gets a mark, so marking all of them means meeting every demand.

clue.text: Eccentric old witch appears first

indicators.note: the witch appears first, so her word stands ahead of the abbreviation for old

parts.note: a weird is an archaic word for a witch or fate-spinner, as in Macbeth's Weird Sisters

explanation.surface: A peculiar old witch makes her entrance before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' is a noun here: an odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric is an oddball, a strange person who behaves unconventionally.

clue.text: Conqueror William's initial secret

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of the name William

parts.note: inner means private or secret, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A hint about William the Conqueror's hidden first letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes William the Conqueror, but 'Conqueror' simply defines a victor.
explanation.definitionFit: A conqueror is one who prevails, a victor.

clue.text: Gershwin from Asian country? Without question

indicators.note: without means the abbreviation for question is removed from the country

parts.note: Iraq is a country in western Asia

explanation.surface: Asking whether the composer Gershwin came from an Asian country, without a doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without question' looks like 'certainly'; it really tells you to drop Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George Gershwin.

clue.text: Nonsense a daughter raised about public school cap

indicators.note: about means the turned letters go around the name of the school
raised in a down clue means the run of letters is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense
Eton is the famous English public school, meaning a private fee-paying one

explanation.surface: A daughter scoffs at a public school cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the nonsense, A and D upwards into DATOR, and 'about' wraps that around the school. A cap here is a small explosive charge, not headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion cap is a small explosive device that sets off a larger charge, which is what a detonator does.

clue.text: A highly seasoned type of sausage unfortunately has to be recalled, note

definitions.text: A highly seasoned type of sausage

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for unfortunately is turned back to front

parts.note: alas expresses that something is unfortunate
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A spicy sausage is unhappily the subject of a product recall.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a strongly spiced cured Italian sausage.

clue.text: I can't see flicks, though I certainly want to!

definitions.text: I can't see flicks, though I certainly want to!

indicators.note: flicks suggests quick movements, so the letters of I can't see are flicked into a new order

explanation.surface: A frustrated film fan laments being unable to get to the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flicks' doubles as slang for films; the anagram of I CANT SEE gives the answer, and the whole clue describes a movie lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is an enthusiast of films, who naturally wants to watch them.

clue.text: Series of letters from one Roman emperor

indicators.note: Series of letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A string of letters taken from a single Roman emperor's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a first-century ruler of the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Passing can, vet seen in new light

indicators.note: seen in a new light means viewed differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tin and a veterinarian glimpsed briefly under fresh lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanescent means fleeting or quickly vanishing, a sense of passing as in a passing fancy.

clue.text: Where a debutante may have been sent for a spell?

definitions.text: Where a debutante may have been sent for a spell?

parts.words: Where a debutante may have been sent for a spell?
parts.note: read one way a young society girl is sent away for a period to learn poise; read the other way a spell is a magic incantation, as at a school of enchantment

explanation.surface: A young society girl packed off for a while to be polished.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing establishments taught young women etiquette and grace before they came out in society.

clue.text: Two kings on board a majestic flagship of yore

indicators.note: on board means the two letters are taken aboard, placed inside the following words

parts.note: royal means regal or majestic
R is short for rex, Latin for king
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Two monarchs travel aboard a grand old naval flagship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts R and K between A and ROYAL. Several Royal Navy flagships, including aircraft carriers, bore this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was borne by the English fleet's lead vessel against the Armada and later by carriers.

clue.text: Ice, mostly, on top of old Irish lake

indicators.note: in a down clue on top of places the first piece above the next
mostly means the word for ice loses its final letter

parts.note: reserve is a cold, icy aloofness of manner

explanation.surface: Ice forming over an old Irish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' means coolness of manner here, RESERVE, cut by 'mostly' to RESERV.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake for storing water.

clue.text: Singer — all things considered, get her off!

indicators.note: off means the words get her are removed from the longer word

parts.note: altogether means on the whole, all things considered
the clue words get her give these letters as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry to drag a singer off the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

clue.text: Bachelor lounged, relaxed in club

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters of lounged are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A single man lounging at ease in his gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gentlemen's club, but 'club' is a heavy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a short thick stick used as a weapon, a cudgel.

clue.text: Backing exploit involving a son of Isaac

indicators.note: involving means the turned word wraps around the letter from a
backing means the word for exploit is turned backwards

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: Supporting a scheme that involves one of Isaac's sons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns USE into ESU, and 'involving' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin sold his birthright to Jacob.

clue.text: Distinctive feature of room, note

parts.note: a hall is a large room
to mark is to note or notice

explanation.surface: The characteristic look of a room, duly noted.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallmark is a characteristic trait, from the official stamp on precious metal.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink, make unknown

parts.note: a make is a brand, as in a make of car
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Producing a drink whose name nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: Dig about journalist being outlawed

indicators.note: about means the word for dig goes around the word for journalist

parts.note: a dig is a poke or prod
a scribe is a writer, informally a journalist

explanation.surface: A dig at a reporter who has been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word. 'Dig' looks like excavation but means a poke.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or ban, so something proscribed is banned by law.

clue.text: Chapter about origin of wedding band

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: origin of takes the first letter of the word wedding

explanation.surface: A chapter on how the wedding band came about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a ring or musicians; it means a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of people is a group or team working together, like a ship's company.

clue.text: Upset soldier in the crew

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters are read backwards
in means the soldier sits inside the word the

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier gets upset among the ship's company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes THGIE, which 'Upset' turns over. An eight is a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat's team of eight oarsmen is itself called by that number in rowing.

clue.text: Struggled, we hear, with what sounds like setbacks in military reservation

indicators.note: we hear means the word for struggled is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: fought means struggled

indicators.note: sounds like means the word for setbacks is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: knocks are setbacks or blows

explanation.surface: A tale of struggle and reverses at an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech fought and fort sound alike. The answer is the US Army post in Kentucky that holds the gold depository.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kentucky site is a US Army post, a military reservation, famed for its bullion vault.

clue.text: Last in retirement home gives money

indicators.note: last in picks out the final letter of the word retirement; that the answer also runs across these two clue words is a coincidence

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Moving into a retirement home brings in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is a British slang word for cash.

clue.text: Sufficient to answer demand in the noughties

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is concealed inside the words the noughties

explanation.surface: Supply keeping pace with demand during the 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means adequate, as much as is needed to satisfy what is required.

clue.text: In goal blocking shot

indicators.note: blocking means the word for goal stands inside the word for shot, obstructing it

parts.note: a try is an attempt, a shot
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football scene: a shot blocked in front of goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the definition, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable, currently in vogue.

clue.text: Columns written about gangster leaving Italy in old age

indicators.note: written about means the word for columns is turned around

parts.note: lines are columns or rows, as in lines of troops

indicators.note: leaving means the gangster's name departs from the word Italy

parts.note: Al Capone was the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Newspaper columns report on an elderly mobster quitting Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' turns LINES into SENIL; 'leaving' removes AL from ITALY to leave ITY; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Senility is the mental decline often associated with advanced years.
